intent:
CI cannot reach the cluster today. Every lab name resolves publicly to
`192.168.2.30`, a private address, so it works only on the LAN or through the
subnet route firebat advertises to the tailnet (`docs/reference/edge-routes.md`,
`.okf/components/tailscale-subnet-router.md`). The only workflows are
GitHub-hosted (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `.github/workflows/claude-ollama.yaml`,
`.github/workflows/hermes-interactive.yaml`). Vault (`vault.lab.orangecluster.nl`)
and the OpenViking API (`openviking-api.lab.orangecluster.nl`) are both behind
HAProxy on `192.168.2.30:443`, so one destination serves the whole ask.

Chosen approach: a GitHub-hosted runner joins the tailnet with the official
`tailscale/github-action` as an ephemeral node tagged `tag:ci`, then logs in
to Vault with its GitHub OIDC token and mints an OpenViking identity token.
GitHub stores no Vault secret. Rejected: a self-hosted runner on the cluster.
The repository is public, and GitHub warns against self-hosted runners on
public repos because a fork's pull request can run code on them. That would
put a code executor on the LAN with no tailnet policy in front of it. Also
rejected: a Tailscale auth key or Vault secret as a repository secret, because
`.github/workflows/claude-ollama.yaml` is an agent with tool use triggered by
issue and PR text, and repository secrets are readable by every workflow.

What changes where:

- **Tailnet policy, in the Tailscale admin console, where it lives today.**
  The repository has no ACL file. Add `tagOwners` for `tag:ci` and one grant
  from `tag:ci` to `192.168.2.30:443` and nothing else. Create a Tailscale
  credential that can only mint ephemeral, pre-approved `tag:ci` nodes:
  workload identity federation bound to this repository if the tailnet
  offers it, otherwise an OAuth client held in a GitHub Environment. The
  policy is the only network control. On firebat, tailscaled's `ts-input`
  chain accepts all `tailscale0` traffic ahead of ufw, and ufw forwards
  routed traffic unfiltered (`.okf/components/host-firewall.md`). The runner
  must accept subnet routes, which `tailscale up` on Linux does not do by
  default, so the action passes `--accept-routes`.
- **Vault, `deployments/infrastructure/machine_roles.tf`** (credentials Vault
  brokers to machines, per `.claude/rules/terraform-file-layout.md`): a JWT
  auth mount `jwt-github` trusting `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`,
  and one role bound to repository `JasperHG90/localstack`, ref
  `refs/heads/main` and the GitHub Environment the workflow uses, with a
  short token TTL. Its one policy reads only its own identity-token path,
  following `vault_policy.openviking_workload`. The MFA enforcement in
  `deployments/infrastructure/identity.tf` names the userpass accessor only,
  so it does not reach the new mount.
- **Vault, `deployments/infrastructure/oidc.tf`**: one
  `vault_identity_oidc_role` for CI on the `identity-tokens` key with audience
  `openviking`, and with `ov_account` and `ov_user` as literals, as
  `vault_identity_oidc_role.openviking_workload` does, because the JWT mount
  owns the entities it creates. A TTL of minutes, not the workloads' month.
- **Workflow, `new:.github/workflows/openviking-sync.yaml`**: runs on push to
  `main` under `docs/` and on `workflow_dispatch`, never on `pull_request`.
  It uses `permissions: id-token: write, contents: read`, a GitHub
  Environment and a timeout. It joins the tailnet, logs in to Vault, mints
  the token, and uploads `docs/` (85 Markdown pages, 1.6 MB today) to one
  fixed `viking://resources/...` target, replacing the previous upload.
- **Knowledge**: update `.okf/components/tailscale-subnet-router.md` with the
  `tag:ci` grant and a read-only copy of the policy stanza (the console stays
  authoritative), and add a decision record for runner choice and
  credentials. A how-to for adding a folder to the sync goes in `docs/how-to/`
  per `.claude/rules/how-to-skeleton.md`.

An earlier plan for the network half alone, C1, is in git at `48f52e2`
(`.loop/plans/C1-cicd-tailscale-github-actions-deploy.md` there). Its points on
GitHub Environments, `workflow_dispatch` and `tagOwners` are carried over.

Outcome: a push to `main` that adds a test page under `docs/` with a unique
marker string runs the workflow. The run joins the tailnet as an ephemeral
`tag:ci` node, which is gone from the console after the run. From the
runner, `https://vault.lab.orangecluster.nl` and
`https://openviking-api.lab.orangecluster.nl` answer, while
`192.168.2.30:8200` and `192.168.2.50:1933` time out. Vault login uses only
the GitHub OIDC token, and the repository and its Environment hold no Vault
credential. The page lands under the target URI, and an OpenViking search
for the marker as `lab`/`jasper` returns it. A `workflow_dispatch` from a
branch other than `main` is refused at the Vault login. `just pre_commit` and
`uv run --directory cli pytest` pass.

## Could invalidate this plan

- Tailnet policy scope. Tailscale's default policy allows every source to
  reach every destination, and tagged nodes match `*`. If the live policy
  still carries such a rule, a `tag:ci` grant adds nothing and the runner
  reaches every tailnet device and the whole LAN through the subnet route,
  every port on firebat included. Fixing that rewrites access for every
  device on the tailnet, which is a scope change the operator must own, not a
  line added for CI. Spike question: does the live tailnet policy let a node
  tagged `tag:ci` reach anything besides `192.168.2.30:443`? With a grant to
  only that destination, does an ephemeral `tag:ci` node reach
  `https://vault.lab.orangecluster.nl` through the subnet route and time out
  on `192.168.2.30:8200` and firebat's tailnet address?
- Remote upload into OpenViking. The sync assumes a client off the cluster
  can send local file contents to `viking://resources/...` with an identity
  token, and that uploading again to the same target replaces the tree
  instead of adding a copy. Hermes only ever adds by URL
  (`deployments/applications/services/hermes/SOUL.md`). If the server takes
  only URLs or server-side paths, the sync has to change shape (OpenViking
  fetching raw GitHub URLs, for instance), and then the tailnet carries only
  the API call. Spike question: against `ghcr.io/jasperhg90/openviking:v0.4.17.1-9`
  in `auth_mode: oidc`, can a remote client upload a local directory of
  Markdown to a fixed `viking://resources/` target with a JWT whose claims are
  literal `ov_account`/`ov_user`? Does uploading it again replace or
  duplicate, and does a search as another user in the same account find it?
